article_content: (CNN) -- Images of mangled remains of crashed passenger planes strike fear into even the hardiest of business travelers. People posing as passengers take part in an anti-terrorist drill at Sukarno-Hatta airport in Jakarta. After a spate of airline emergencies, CNN's Business Traveller examines the risks of plane travel and investigates ways to make journeys safer. British Airways offers a safety course once reserved for pilots and cabin crew, which takes place in a hangar at London's Heathrow airport. Barry Leonard, a passenger on US Airways Flight 1549, shares how these procedures saved his life. The show also explores security measures at luxury hotels like the Oberoi in Mumbai and the Adlon Kempinski in Berlin. It looks at high-security fashion by Miguel Caballero, known as the 'Armani of Bullet-proof Apparel'.

Des personnes simulant des passagers participent à un exercice anti-terroriste à l'aéroport Sukarno-Hatta à Jakarta. Après plusieurs urgences aériennes, CNN's Business Traveller examine les risques du voyage aérien et les moyens de les réduire. British Airways propose un cours de sécurité anciennement réservé aux pilotes et au personnel de cabine à l'aéroport Heathrow de Londres. Barry Leonard, passager du vol US Airways 1549, raconte comment ces procédures lui ont sauvé la vie. L'émission explore les mesures de sécurité dans les hôtels de luxe comme l'Oberoi à Mumbai et l'Adlon Kempinski à Berlin, ainsi que la mode de haute sécurité de Miguel Caballero, 'l'Armani du vêtement pare-balles'.

article_content: Jeremy Clarkson has sparked controversy after claiming that people in Liverpool 'earn less, die more quickly, and have fewer jobs' compared to those in the South of England. The 'Top Gear' host made these comments after visiting the city for one of his programme's live shows, describing local houses as being 'worth the square root of sod all'. The mayor of Liverpool, Joe Anderson, has responded by labelling Clarkson an 'oaf and a buffoon'. Clarkson's comments were made during the 'Top Gear Live' tour, where he also mocked a local restaurant and hotel for staff not knowing what a 'kipper' or 'Tabasco sauce' were. He further shared some negative experiences from previous visits, including hearing constant burglar alarms and witnessing a knifeman 'run amok' in a restaurant. The mayor has announced plans to complain to the BBC about Clarkson's remarks, which were published in his 'Sunday Times' column.

Les commentaires de Clarkson ont été faits lors de la tournée 'Top Gear Live', où il a également critiqué un restaurant et un hôtel locaux. Le maire a annoncé son intention de se plaindre à la BBC.

article_content: Headteachers are advising parents to reduce their phone usage to make their children feel heard. Parents should stop checking their mobiles and listen to their children when they're talking, headteachers said. Bernadette Hunter, president of the 'National Association of Head Teachers', noted that it's 'easy for everyone, even parents, to be distracted by the immediacy of electronic communications.' The advice comes in a leaflet by the NAHT and Family Action charity, aimed at helping parents develop their child's speaking and listening skills. It suggests giving children attention, switching off screens before bedtime, and having family meals together.
translated_content: Les directeurs d'école conseillent aux parents de réduire leur utilisation du téléphone pour que leurs enfants se sentent entendus. Les parents devraient cesser de consulter leur téléphone portable et écouter leurs enfants lorsqu'ils leur parlent, ont déclaré les directeurs d'école. Bernadette Hunter, présidente de l'Association nationale des directeurs d'école, a souligné qu'il est 'facile pour tout le monde, même les parents, d'être distrait par l'immédiateté des communications électroniques.' Le dépliant de la NAHT et de l'organisme de bienfaisance Family Action vise à aider les parents à développer les compétences de leurs enfants en matière de parole et d'écoute. Il suggère de donner toute leur attention aux enfants, d'éteindre les écrans avant le coucher et de partager des repas en famille.

article_content: 'The Wave', a natural marvel hidden deep within Arizona's desert, resembles a Martian landscape. This 190 million-year-old geological formation is composed of ancient sand dunes that have transformed into rock. The unique layering is a result of calcium salt deposits hardening the stacked sand dunes. Located in the Vermillion Cliffs Wilderness Area, accessing 'The Wave' requires a special permit and a three-mile hike. Photographer Justin Reznick described his experience as surreal, highlighting the formation's unique sandstone patterns and beauty.
translated_content: 'La Vague', une merveille naturelle cachée dans le désert de l'Arizona, ressemble à un paysage martien. Cette formation géologique de 190 millions d'années est faite d'anciennes dunes de sable transformées en roche. La stratification unique résulte de dépôts de sels de calcium qui ont durci les dunes empilées. Située dans la zone sauvage des Vermillion Cliffs, l'accès nécessite un permis spécial et une randonnée de trois miles. Le photographe Justin Reznick a décrit son expérience comme surréaliste, soulignant les motifs de grès et la beauté de la formation.

article_content: Zaria Forman, a 31-year-old artist from Brooklyn, New York, creates hyper-realistic finger paintings that capture landscapes affected by climate change. Her works, taking up to a month to complete, document the beauty of regions like the Arctic. Forman led an Arctic expedition to Greenland's northwest coast, inspired by the geography and fulfilling a promise to her late mother, Rena Bass Forman. Trained at Skidmore College, Forman's art is featured in U.S. and international galleries, including set designs for 'Giselle' and 'House of Cards'. Priced between $6,000 and $9,000, her paintings realistically depict icy landscapes and ocean scenes.

Ses œuvres, qui nécessitent jusqu'à un mois de travail, capturent la beauté changeante de régions comme l'Arctique. Forman a dirigé une expédition arctique sur la côte nord-ouest du Groenland, s'inspirant de la géographie spectaculaire et honorant une promesse faite à sa mère, Rena Bass Forman, disparue. Diplômée du Skidmore College, les créations de Forman sont exposées dans des galeries américaines et internationales, notamment pour les décors de 'Giselle' et 'House of Cards'. Ses peintures, vendues entre 6 000 $ et 9 000 $, représentent avec un réalisme saisissant des paysages de glace et des scènes marines.

Federal authorities have temporarily restricted flights over a wooded area near the Irwin's home as authorities continue their search. Deborah Bradley, Lisa's mother, initially said she checked on Lisa at 10:30 PM but later clarified that she hadn't checked on her after putting her to bed at 6:30 PM. The parents haven't been questioned by police in the last ten days, which has drawn criticism from law enforcement.

article_content: The Chicago Teachers Union announced that its over 26,000 teachers and support staff will go on strike on Monday for the first time in 25 years. The union stated that contract talks with the district failed late Sunday night over issues including benefits and job security. 'We will be on the picket line,' Chicago Teachers Union President Karen Lewis said Sunday night, calling it a 'difficult decision'. The union's members are expected to hit the picket lines on Monday morning. School board President David Vitale announced that talks had broken off despite the school board offering a four-year contract worth $400 million. The city has a contingency plan with 144 public schools open to students from 8:30am to 12:30pm. Regular school transportation won't be available; parents are responsible for their children's transportation and registration on the district's website.

Les membres du syndicat sont attendus sur les lignes de piquetage lundi matin. Le président du conseil scolaire, David Vitale, a annoncé que les discussions avaient échoué malgré l'offre d'un contrat de quatre ans d'une valeur de 400 millions de dollars. article_content: It's becoming increasingly likely that Darren Wilson, the police officer who shot Michael Brown in Ferguson, Missouri, won't face criminal charges. The state grand jury decided not to indict Wilson, and recent news suggests that federal charges won't be filed either. These decisions highlight the challenges of using criminal cases to drive large-scale reform. Criminal investigations focus on specific events, like Brown's death, but the details surrounding the incident remain unclear. The confrontation between Brown and Wilson is disputed, with questions about who was the aggressor and whether Brown's actions justified the fatal shots. While these questions are crucial for determining Wilson's guilt, they don't shed much light on broader issues like police interactions with African-Americans and community safety. Using individual cases like Brown's and Eric Garner's as symbols for larger societal issues can be misleading. The criminal law works best when it's tied to the facts of a specific case, treating defendants equally without singling them out as symbols of larger problems. The decision not to charge Wilson shouldn't be seen as vindication for him or the police force; it's a reflection of the high standards for criminal prosecutions. There's still much work to be done to address societal issues, regardless of the outcome for individual cases.

Le grand jury d'État a décidé de ne pas inculper Wilson, et des informations récentes suggèrent que des accusations fédérales ne seront pas non plus déposées. Ces décisions soulignent les défis liés à l'utilisation des affaires pénales pour conduire des réformes à grande échelle. Les enquêtes pénales se concentrent sur des événements spécifiques, comme la mort de Brown, mais les détails entourant l'incident restent flous. La confrontation entre Brown et Wilson est contestée, avec des questions sur qui était l'agresseur et si les actions de Brown ont justifié les tirs mortels. Bien que ces questions soient cruciales pour déterminer la culpabilité de Wilson, elles n'éclairent guère sur des questions plus larges comme les interactions entre la police et les Afro-Américains et la sécurité communautaire. Utiliser des cas individuels comme ceux de Brown et Eric Garner comme symboles de problèmes sociétaux plus larges peut être trompeur. Le droit pénal fonctionne mieux lorsqu'il est lié aux faits d'une affaire spécifique, traitant les accusés de manière égale sans les distinguer comme symboles de problèmes plus vastes. La décision de ne pas inculper Wilson ne devrait pas être considérée comme une justification pour lui ou la force de police; c'est le reflet des normes élevées pour les poursuites pénales. Il reste encore beaucoup à faire pour résoudre les problèmes sociétaux, quel que soit le résultat pour les cas individuels.

article_content: Workers are cutting out the traditional 'brew after work', a practice that's falling flat with bar owners. The 2008-2009 recession led to slower traffic at some bars and sluggish beer sales nationwide. According to The Beer Institute, US beer drinkers consumed 203.4 million barrels last year, about 5% less than in 2008. 'Beer drinkers are pretty responsible people,' said Chris Thorne, vice president of communications at The Beer Institute. The high-end craft beer segment saw a 14% sales increase in the first half of 2012 compared to the same period last year.

article_content: Rene Gonzalez, one of the 'Cuban Five', was released on Friday after serving most of his 15-year sentence for spying, a prison spokesman told CNN. Gonzalez was convicted in 2001 for spying on Cuban-American exile leaders and U.S. military bases as part of the 'Wasp Network'. He was arrested in 1998 and served 13 years and 26 days. Gonzalez still has three years of probation. His attorney, Philip Horowitz, said Gonzalez will appeal to serve his probation in Cuba. Gonzalez's release is bittersweet as his four colleagues remain in prison. He has a 25-year-old daughter and a 13-year-old daughter who was four months old when he was arrested.

article_content: In the heart of Zanzibar's historic Stone Town, a vibrant shop stands out among the rest. Aromas of Zanzibar, founded by 29-year-old Rizwan Janmohamed, is a haven for locally crafted clothing and accessories. Every item, from guitar cases to cosmetic bags, is made on site by local artisans using materials sourced from the island. Janmohamed's vision was to create something authentically Zanzibari, a departure from the imported goods that dominated the local market. With the help of a bank loan and support from family and friends, Janmohamed turned his dream into a reality after leaving his job as a hotel assistant manager. The shop attracts thousands of tourists looking for a genuine piece of Zanzibar to take home. Janmohamed's products, such as colorful Kitenge print wallets and spice-infused teas, showcase the island's rich cultural heritage. Despite initial challenges, Janmohamed's business is now breaking even, with plans to turn a profit within two years. He attributes his success to the unique blend of Swahili and Arabian cultures in Zanzibar's handicrafts and a commitment to customer service.

article_content: A new trend is emerging in the UK where recently divorced individuals are turning to 'revenge plastic surgery' to transform their bodies and potentially make their ex-partners jealous. According to Transform Plastic Surgery Group, 26% of their patients are recently divorced women, and 11% are recently divorced men, marking a rise from the previous year. The procedures range from non-invasive treatments like fillers and Botox to more invasive surgeries such as full body lifts and breast implants. This trend, which has been prevalent in the U.S. for years, is now gaining traction in the UK. Many individuals feel they 'let themselves go' during their marriage and, upon re-entering the dating scene, experience a crisis of confidence. Top plastic surgeon Dr. Brent Moelleken advises that having plastic surgery for someone else's benefit is not recommended, stating it's 'part of the grieving process when a relationship ends.'

article_content: John F. Kennedy, elected in '60, wasn't initially set on changing the world. He criticized Eisenhower's administration for not prosecuting the Cold War vigorously. Kennedy believed 'Massive Retaliation' left America unable to respond to non-nuclear aggression. He aimed to close the 'missile gap' and be first on the moon. Initially, Kennedy was cautious on civil rights, relying on moderate southern leaders. However, after several crises, he shifted his stance. The Bay of Pigs failure didn't deter him from covert actions, but after confronting the Soviets over Berlin and Cuba, he eased Cold War tensions. Kennedy started secret talks with Khrushchev and negotiated the Test Ban Treaty, a significant step towards détente. At home, he proposed a tax cut despite a budget deficit. Violent resistance to civil rights protests forced Kennedy to act, sending federal troops to the University of Mississippi and promising strong civil rights legislation. Kennedy's assassination led to LBJ continuing some policies, including the civil rights bill. It's debated whether Kennedy would have withdrawn from Vietnam; his '63 actions suggest commitment to South Vietnam. Kennedy's memory resonates today, perhaps due to current American politics being dysfunctional.

article_content: (CNN) -- One of 'No Child Left Behind's' controversial initiatives -- support for single-sex public schools and classes -- has come under heavy fire from critics. A common objection is that the programs are based on gender stereotypes: 'Boys need discipline and should be free to run around the classroom; girls require gentle care and can be trusted to sit still.' Is single-sex public education outdated and backward? Sociologist Michael Kimmel wrote that single-sex classrooms 'segregate boys and girls.' Segregation usually calls to mind racial segregation. In public schools today, black students remain more segregated from white students compared with other racial and ethnic groups. But does separating students by gender do more harm than good? Separation is not always segregation. Some single-sex schools can do more good than harm. For educators looking to address the needs of black boys -- who lag behind their peers on academic and social measures -- single-sex education is an important tool. Take Urban Charter, a school I researched for a year. (Urban Charter is a pseudonym due to federal guidelines.) It's an all-boys high school on the East Coast. Nearly all the boys are African-American, and most of their families are working-class or poor. Opponents warn that single-sex schools reinforce gender stereotypes. Yet Urban Charter's teachers fought stereotypes, nurturing individual interests and passions. Critics worry that all-boys schools promote a machismo culture. Yet the school's commitment to helping young men become gentlemen included lessons on respecting women and girls. The school's founder said, 'Separation gives you an opportunity to work with the boys.' This opportunity was in creating a pro-academic climate with small class sizes and a longer school day. Urban Charter's accomplishments are notable: a near-perfect graduation rate since 2011, and over 80% of students going on to college. Research shows single-sex schools serving at-risk youth succeed for reasons beyond just gender separation. Parents should have the option to choose between single-sex and coeducational programs, as per 2006 Department of Education guidelines. Proponents sometimes use biological sex differences to justify single-sex education. But Urban Charter focused on real differences in academic and social outcomes between black boys and their peers. Single-sex public education can be empowering, particularly for African-American boys.

La ségrégation évoque la ségrégation raciale. Mais la séparation par genre fait-elle plus de mal que de bien ? Pour les éducateurs, l'éducation mono-sexe est un outil important pour les garçons noirs. Urban Charter, un lycée pour garçons sur la côte est, en est un exemple. Les enseignants ont combattu les stéréotypes et encouragé les passions individuelles. L'école a obtenu un taux de diplomation quasi-parfait et plus de 80% des élèves ont poursuivi leurs études. Les parents devraient avoir le choix entre les programmes mono-sexes et mixtes, selon les directives du Département de l'Éducation de 2006. L'éducation mono-sexe peut être empowering, particulièrement pour les garçons afro-américains.

article_content: AUSTIN, TEXAS - There's a new trend sweeping across cultures and continents: robot baristas. A tech company in Austin is revolutionizing the coffee experience with robots that make coffee just like humans. For '$1 more than Starbucks', you can get your coffee made by a robot. This robot barista solves a 'pressing global problem', said Charles Studor, Briggo's founder and CEO. 'Coffee is ubiquitous... we're solving a common global problem: high-quality, convenient, consistent coffee that's efficient with beans and raw materials,' Studor said. Customers can download the Briggo app, customize their order, and pick it up when it's ready. 'It's perfect for avoiding lines,' said Astrid Chacon, who tried a robot-made coffee. 'We're often wasteful in the West... we want to connect consumers with the origin of quality beans,' Studor said. Studor's goal is to create social impact by connecting consumers with coffee growers through 'direct blockchain technology'. 'Maybe farmers have issues... we can connect you to help with projects,' Studor said. While big-name brands like Starbucks help farming communities, will robot baristas with a social cause threaten traditional cafes?
